title: Giant Batch Lasagna
subtitle: Feeds 12+ without drama
description: Feeds 12+ without drama. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Giant Batch Lasagna in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Yellow onion, diced as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown meat sauce
steps.instruction: Brown beef and sausage with onion and garlic. Add crushed tomatoes and marinara; simmer 20 minutes until thick. Season with Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Mix ricotta filling
steps.instruction: Stir ricotta with eggs, half the parmesan, salt, and pepper until smooth. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Cook lasagna sheets
steps.instruction: Boil lasagna noodles in salted water until pliable; drain and lay flat on oiled sheet pans so they do not stick. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Layer in hotel pans
steps.instruction: Spread meat sauce, noodles, ricotta dollops, mozzarella, and repeat. Finish with sauce and cheese on top — batch lasagna is layered, not tossed in a pot.

steps.title: Bake covered then brown
steps.instruction: Bake covered at 375°F 45 minutes, then uncover and bake 15–20 minutes until bubbling and golden. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Rest and cut squares
steps.instruction: Rest 15 minutes before cutting so layers hold. Serve squares from the pan for crew portions. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Firefighters eat heavy after rough nights — double the protein if the hall had a busy shift.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Giant Batch Lasagna with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Serve family-style from two full-size trays — never let the line run dry on a busy night.
Put starch and protein on separate trays so vegetarians can load up on sides.
Line up Giant Batch Lasagna on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Feeds 12+ without drama. A hall pick for big-appetite nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Giant Batch Lasagna runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
